_comment: The approval authority for Dockerfile base/tool image pins (#349). Every digest-pinned image reference in any Dockerfile must appear here with the exact same image, tag and digest, and every pin row must still be referenced by at least one Dockerfile -- the registry and the tree hold each other closed, so a base update is always a reviewable change to this file plus the Dockerfiles. A pin reference is `name:tag@sha256:<digest>`: the digest is the resolution authority (immutable), the tag is the human-readable version annotation. All digests below are the manifest-list (index) digests the named tag resolved to on `recorded`, so every architecture/platform variant of that tag is fixed by one pin and a fixed target platform always resolves to the same per-arch artifact. Checked by scripts/check-image-pins.py, which also rejects any `:latest` reference and any unexempted unpinned base. `exemptions` exist for INTERNAL images that intentionally keep a version tag; each must name an owner, an issue and a reason, exactly like quality/image-inventory.json's coverage exceptions -- an exemption nobody owns is just an exemption.

pins.note: CPython 3.13.16 on Debian bookworm-slim; the interpreter pin that keeps coincurve building from source only on purpose. Refreshed from 3.13.15 (#363): the grype leg of the container gate flags CPython binary HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs (CVE-2026-19445/19553/82049) whose fixes landed in 3.13.16. Digest refreshed 2026-10-22 (#1152): security.yml run 39823108438 flags libexpat1 2.5.0-1+deb12u4 (CVE-2025-59375 / CVE-2026-77214, HIGH, fixed 2.5.0-1+deb12u5) in maistro-engine because the buildx gha cache still serves the pre-upgrade `apt-get upgrade` layer; the base-digest bump invalidates that cached layer so the rebuilt image upgrades to deb12u5 (locally verified: fresh builds already resolved deb12u5, so only the cached-CI layer was stale).

CPython 3.12.x line as of the recording date (resolves to 3.12.15); research, RSI runner, e2e and sbx-tests images. Refreshed (#363): the grype leg of the container gate flags CPython binary HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs fixed in 3.12.15. Digest refreshed 2026-10-24 (#93): security.yml runs 40081082641/40088232144/40091186336 flag libbrotli1 1.1.0-2+b7 (CVE-2026-111497, HIGH, fixed 1.1.0-2+deb13u1 / DSA-6582-1) in maistro-rsi-runner even though the same runs' build logs show the re-executed apt stage installing 1.1.0-2+deb13u1 — buildx cache keys are computed pre-execution from the instruction string and parent key chain, never from a RUN's fresh bytes, so `--no-cache-filter runtime-apt` re-executes the stage but cannot stop the downstream stages from reusing pre-advisory cache chains (and mode=max cached manifests) that carry the old OS layer into the loaded image. The base-digest bump changes the key chain from the FROM down, so the rebuilt image assembles the freshly executed layers (same doctrine as the 3.13.16-slim-bookworm #1152 refresh).

The mutable tag has since advanced to a newer index; this row preserves the reviewed immutable Dependabot pin. The single-tenant template retains its separate 3.12.12 pin.

Builds the age static binaries and the static docker CLI from their pinned upstream release tags (#363, then #1152): the published docker:29-cli binary embeds go1.26.8 stdlib and the age prebuilt binary go1.25.x, both carrying 2026 stdlib HIGHs (CVE-2026-78667/78669/97031, fixed in go1.26.9/1.27.2) that no released tag of either project ships fixed. The 1.27.2 rebuild then aged out itself: CVE-2026-111943 (crypto/x509 MITM via untrusted intermediate certificates, HIGH, fixed in go1.26.10/1.27.3) flagged both binaries' stdlib, so the builder moved to 1.27.3-alpine — #1095's trunk-CI repair independently hit the same advisory and re-resolved the same tag to this identical digest. Resolved 2026-10-22 hours after upstream re-serialized the tag's index with unchanged per-arch content (the earlier same-day index d530cf60723abf1ffae0cd16bb546b379ec0550d2f3815e5b16ed69dbc00fba4 carries the identical linux/amd64 child). The same 1.27.2 -> 1.27.3 bump was independently required by the #795 container-cache repair lane, whose Container scan gate flagged the identical CVE on the age/age-keygen and docker CLI binaries.

uv 0.12.21, verified by running `uv --version` from the image the :latest tag resolved to on the recording date; the tag was rewritten from :latest to the release it actually was. The API image and the Conductor image join this list with #348: both now install their Python dependency set from the committed uv.lock through this pinned uv, so the installer that resolves the shipped set is itself immutable.
